title: Frittata di Pasta
subtitle: Neapolitan fried pasta omelette with leftover spaghetti
excerpt: Frittata di pasta is a Neapolitan way of using leftover cooked spaghetti: mixed with beaten eggs, parmesan, and black pepper, then fried in a pan until set and crisp on both sides. It is golden outside and tender inside, and it eats completely differently from the original pasta dish.
sourceNotes: Frittata di pasta is a Neapolitan cucina povera classic, designed to use up leftover pasta rather than waste it. It appears in Jeanne Carola Francesconi's comprehensive collection of Neapolitan cooking, La Cucina Napoletana (1965), as a standard home preparation. The dish is also made throughout Campania with a variety of pasta shapes.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Serve hot from the pan. Can be made 1 hour ahead and served at room temperature in slices.

content.text: Frittata di pasta is the Neapolitan way to use leftover spaghetti. The cold pasta is mixed with beaten eggs, parmesan, and black pepper, then fried in olive oil in a flat pan until the outside is crisp and golden and the egg is set all the way through. It is flipped once and crisped on the second side. The result is dense and savoury, completely different from the original pasta dish even if made from the same leftovers.

items.prepNote: cooked and cooled, leftover is ideal

content.text: Beat the eggs in a large bowl with the parmesan, black pepper, and a small pinch of salt.
Add the cold spaghetti and toss to coat it in the egg mixture. It should look well covered.
Heat the olive oil in a 26 to 28 cm frying pan over medium heat. Add the pasta mixture and press it flat with a spatula to fill the pan in an even layer.
Cook undisturbed for 6 to 8 minutes until the base is golden and the frittata is set about halfway up the sides.

Place a large flat plate over the pan. Flip the frittata onto the plate, then slide it back into the pan uncooked-side down. Cook for a further 5 to 6 minutes until the second side is golden and the frittata is set all the way through.
Slide onto a board and cut into wedges. Eat hot or at room temperature.

Frittata di pasta is Neapolitan cucina povera: the cooking of making the most of what is already in the house. In Naples, leftover pasta of any kind is treated as an ingredient rather than something to reheat and eat again the same way. The frittata form turns it into something new. It is also a popular street snack in Naples, cut into squares and sold from trays.
